core_obligations: Reduce, using the section on intrinsic properties, to a morphism of ringed sites (f, f^sharp) whose underlying functor u : D -> C is left exact and continuous between sites having all finite limits (proof lines 3466-3471).

Let G be a module on D with one of the local properties (1)-(6) of the definition; use that D has a final object Y with X = u(Y) final in C, and choose a covering {Y_i -> Y} such that G restricted to D/Y_i has the corresponding global property (proof lines 3472-3479).

Set X_i = u(Y_i) so that {X_i -> X} is a covering in C, and exploit the displayed commutative diagram of morphisms of ringed sites to compare the localizations and transfer the global property to f^*G (proof lines 3480-3498).
Conclude that each of the seven listed local properties is preserved under pullback, including quasi-coherence and finite presentation.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case of a left exact continuous functor between sites with finite limits.
Choose a covering on which the module has the corresponding global property.
Transfer the property through the diagram of localizations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that pullback along a morphism of ringed topoi preserves seven local properties of modules: locally free, finite locally free, locally generated by sections, locally generated by r sections, finite type, quasi-coherent, and finite presentation. The proof reduces, via the discussion of intrinsic properties, to morphisms of ringed sites given by a left exact continuous functor u between sites with all finite limits; it then takes a module with one of the local properties, uses the final object and a covering {Y_i -> Y} on which the restriction has the corresponding global property, sets X_i = u(Y_i) to get a covering in the source site, and compares the resulting commutative diagram of localizations to transfer the global property, whence the local one (proof lines 3466-3498). H2: the reduction to the left exact continuous case and the transfer through the diagram of localizations are the substance.
